item.title: Overview
item.description:
The open source manager for the infrastructure you run

If you build and run the internal platform your developers ship on, you already know the shape of the problem: many clusters, more than one cloud, and a long tail of cloud native tools that each speak their own dialect. Meshery is the open source, cloud native manager that gives you one place to design, operate, and characterize all of it.

item.title: Quick Start Guide
item.description:
Meshery runs as a set of containers on either a Kubernetes cluster or a Docker host. This guide installs Meshery’s command line interface, mesheryctl, and uses it to start Meshery Server, then walks you through signing in and connecting your clusters.

Quick Start Assumptions

This guide downloads, installs, and runs Meshery with a single command, and assumes that your current kubeconfig context points at the cluster you want to use. For instructions specific to your environment, see all supported platforms.

item.title: Using Meshery Playground
item.description:
Try out Meshery Playground at https://playground.meshery.io/

Meshery Playground is a web-based, collaborative environment where you can explore Meshery and the infrastructure it manages, including multiple Kubernetes clusters, CNCF projects, applications, services, and operators that run on Kubernetes. The Playground gives you a sandbox for experimenting with infrastructure configurations and deployment options, and its multiplayer features let you design and operate infrastructure in real time with your teammates.

item.title: Upgrading Meshery
item.description:
Upgrade Guide

Meshery is a composition of components that upgrade in a specific order: the CLI first, the Server second, and the components on managed clusters - Meshery Operator, MeshSync, and Broker - automatically, driven by the Server. You do not upgrade the Operator by hand. This page explains how the components version in relation to one another and walks through the upgrade procedure, verification, and rollback. For production practices (pinned versions, upgrade-friendly probes, rollback rehearsal), see the Operational Readiness Checklist.

item.title: Accessing Meshery UI
item.description:
Accessing Meshery UI

Once Meshery is running, mesheryctl system start opens Meshery UI in your default browser. On Docker, Meshery UI listens at http://localhost:9081 by default. On Kubernetes, mesheryctl opens the address of the meshery service in the meshery namespace, which the Helm chart creates as a LoadBalancer service on port 9081.

To open Meshery UI in your default browser at any time, run:


mesheryctl system dashboard

If your cluster does not give the meshery service a reachable address, forward a local port to Meshery instead. By default, mesheryctl listens on local port 9081; use -p to choose another port.
